decisions.question: e-12154

source.question: e-12154
source.value:
The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

$$
x_{n+1} = x_n - \dfrac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}
$$

where $f'(x_n)$ is the derivative of $f(x)$ evaluated at $x_n.$

In our case, we have

$$
f'(x) = (5^{2x}-20)' = 2\ln (5)\cdot 5^{2x}.
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{{5}^{2{x}_{n}}-20}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)\cdot {5}^{2{x}_{n}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with $x_0 = 1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-\frac{{5}^{2{x}_{0}}-20}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)\cdot {5}^{2{x}_{0}}}. \\  & =1-\frac{{5}^{2}-20}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)\cdot {5}^{2}}. \\  & ≈0.938,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.

source.value:
The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

$$
x_{n+1} = x_n - \dfrac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}
$$

where $f'(x_n)$ is the derivative of $f(x)$ evaluated at $x_n.$

In our case, we have

$$
f'(x) = (e^x-x^3-3)' = e^x-3x^2.
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{{e}^{{x}_{n}}-{x}_{n}^{3}-3}{{e}^{{x}_{n}}-3{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with $x_0 = 5,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-\frac{{e}^{{x}_{0}}-{x}_{0}^{3}-3}{{e}^{{x}_{0}}-3{x}_{0}^{2}} \\  & =5-\frac{{e}^{5}-{5}^{3}-3}{{e}^{5}-3(5)^{2}} \\  & =4.721\,941…\end{aligned}
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-\frac{{e}^{{x}_{1}}-{x}_{1}^{3}-3}{{e}^{{x}_{1}}-3{x}_{1}^{2}} \\  & =(4.721\,941…)-\frac{{e}^{4.721\,941…}-(4.721\,941…)^{3}-3}{{e}^{4.721\,941…}-3(4.721\,941…)^{2}} \\  & ≈4.632,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.

source.question: e-12156
source.value:
The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

$$
x_{n+1} = x_n - \dfrac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}
$$

where $f'(x_n)$ is the derivative of $f(x)$ evaluated at $x_n.$

In our case, we have

$$
f'(x) = (x^5-2)' = 5x^4.
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{{x}_{n}^{5}-2}{5{x}_{n}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{{x}_{n}(5{x}_{n}^{4})-({x}_{n}^{5}-2)}{5{x}_{n}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{4{x}_{n}^{5}+2}{5{x}_{n}^{4}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with $x_0 = 1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{4{x}_{0}^{5}+2}{5{x}_{0}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{4(1)^{5}+2}{5(1)^{4}} \\  & =\frac{6}{5} \\  & =1.2.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\frac{4{x}_{1}^{5}+2}{5{x}_{1}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{4(1.2)^{5}+2}{5(1.2)^{4}} \\  & =1.152… \\ {x}_{3} & =\frac{4{x}_{2}^{5}+2}{5{x}_{2}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{4(1.152…)^{5}+2}{5(1.152…)^{4}} \\  & =1.148….\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the last two approximations $x_2 \approx 1.15$ and $x_3 \approx 1.15$ are the same when rounded to two decimal places.

Therefore, the root of the function is $x \approx 1.15,$ rounded to two decimal places.
